content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the process of catalytic and steam cracking
Describe the petrochemical industry and its products

is the process of breaking down long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones. This is essential because fractional distillation produces more long-chain hydrocarbons than are needed, while demand for short-chain fuels and alkenes is high.
Break long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter ones
Converts excess fuel oil into petrol and diesel
Also produces alkenes for making plastics
Breaking C-C bonds in long-chain alkanes
Requires high temperatures and often a catalyst
Products include at least one alkene
Include alkenes, aromatics, and their derivatives
Write a balanced equation for the cracking of dodecane (C₁₂H₂₆) to produce octane and one other product.
Describe the conditions for catalytic cracking.
Long-chain hydrocarbons are passed over the hot catalyst
C-C bonds break to form shorter chains
Products include shorter alkanes and alkenes
The catalyst provides a surface for the reaction and lowers activation energy
Explain why cracking is important for the petrochemical industry.
Crude oil produces too many long-chain hydrocarbons
There is high demand for short-chain fuels like petrol
Cracking converts excess heavy fractions to petrol and diesel
Alkenes are not found in crude oil directly
Name two products that can be made from ethene and explain why ethene is such an important chemical.
Used for plastic bags, bottles, containers
Made by hydration of ethene with steam
Used as solvent, fuel, and in drinks (via fermentation)
It is the most produced organic chemical
It contains a reactive C=C double bond
It is the starting material for many industrial processes
Without ethene, we couldn't make most plastics
Cracking produces shorter alkanes AND alkenes
Not balancing carbons and hydrogens in cracking equations
Both must balance; check your working
Thinking steam cracking uses steam as a reactant
Steam is used to dilute and carry the hydrocarbons; it doesn't react
Explain why cracking is carried out on long-chain hydrocarbons. (3 marks)
Write a balanced equation for the cracking of C₁₄H₃₀ to produce C₈H₁₈, C₂H₄, and one other product. (3 marks)
Describe the conditions for catalytic cracking. (3 marks)
State two uses for ethene produced by cracking. (2 marks)
Compare catalytic cracking and steam cracking. (4 marks)
Explain the environmental problems associated with the petrochemical industry. (3 marks)
Breaking down long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter ones
Cracking using a zeolite catalyst at ~500°C
Cracking at high temperature (~850°C) with steam
Aluminosilicate catalyst used in catalytic cracking
Breaking down a compound using heat
Too many long-chain hydrocarbons; need short ones for fuels and alkenes
Most important petrochemical, makes poly(ethene), ethanol, many other products
Non-renewable resources, plastic pollution, greenhouse gases
